This is the first application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) for grant of anticipatory bail apprehending his arrest in relation to Crime No.39/2023 registered at Police Station - Ashoka Garden, District Bhopal (M.P.)
for the offence punishable under Section 363, 366-A, 376, 376(2)(n), 376(2)(), 370, 419, 120-B of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.

sentences.text: 2. As per the prosecution story, the co-accused persons have involved in the business of prostitution.
They have indulged the prosecutrix into the said business.
During investigation, the applicant has been made accused on the basis of memorandum of co-accused.
Therefore, the offence has been registered against the present applicant and co-accused persons under the aforesaid section.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.

It is submitted that in the FIR as well as statements of prosecutrix under Section 161 &
164 of Cr.P.C., name of present applicant is not mentioned.
He has been made accused only on the basis of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42642 2 MCRC-26148-2025 memorandum of co-accused.
The conclusion of trial will take considerable time.
In these circumstances, applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant and has submitted that the applicant is involved in the alleged crime.

He has actively participated alongwith co-accused persons for business of selling and trading several girls.
He is absconding for longtime.

The applicant has also criminal antecedents of two cases; one is registered at Crime No.50/2025 in P.S. Ashoka Garden, Bhopal and the other at Crime No.313/2023 in P.S. Udaypura,
District Raisen, Bhopal.
Hence, the applicant does not deserve grant of anticipatory bail.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.
Looking to aforesaid facts and circumstances as well as act of present applicant and seriousness of the offence, I am not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
7. Accordingly, present MCRC stands dismissed.
